requirement: Responses to HEAD contain no content.
notes: HTTP/1 cases; HTTP/2 is inventoried separately.

requirement: Successful CONNECT switches to tunnel mode instead of carrying ordinary response content.
notes: The target API lacks an explicit tunnel handle; cannot claim bidirectional tunnel observation.

requirement: Informational responses contain no content.
notes: Existing interim-response cases need independent API-versus-wire audit; server interim emission is unavailable in the frozen scenario contract.

requirement: 204 responses contain no content.
notes: HTTP/1 framing coverage; HTTP/2 is inventoried separately.

requirement: 304 responses contain no content.
notes: HTTP/1 framing coverage; HTTP/2 is inventoried separately.

requirement: Other responses may carry zero-length content.
notes: Zero content is distinct from a special bodyless response; server case also exercises a zero-length request.

requirement: Method, status, and fields determine the application meaning of content.
notes: Application representation semantics and multipart range content are outside wire scope.

requirement: HEAD, 204, and 304 content identification starts with their absence of response content.
notes: Only framing consequences are in scope.

requirement: Content-Location and response metadata identify representations.
notes: Resource identity, trust, and representation selection are application semantics.

requirement: The target URI excludes the URI reference fragment.
notes: Need sender cases for fragment removal in both protocol mappings without URI-adapter normalization hiding the behavior.

requirement: Request control data and Host convey the components required to identify the target.
notes: Representative target forms are tested, but complete origin/authority reconstruction across mappings remains explicitly incomplete.

requirement: CONNECT uses host and port separated by a colon.
notes: Frozen request URI API requires an authority-form fidelity audit before claiming sender coverage.

requirement: OPTIONS may use the asterisk request target.
notes: Sender observation currently provisional; URI adapter fidelity is reviewed separately.

requirement: CONNECT and asterisk target forms are not generated for other methods.
notes: No sender matrix for non-CONNECT authority-form and non-OPTIONS asterisk-form; a sender prohibition alone does not invent mandatory server rejection.

requirement: Servers reconstruct target URI according to protocol version and local connection context.
notes: The observation contract exposes a path but not every reconstructed scheme/authority decision.

requirement: Connection is a list of token-valued connection options.
notes: Lifecycle cases sample close options; complete list grammar, empty member boundaries, and generic option-token generation are not exhausted.

requirement: Connection options are case-insensitive.
notes: Lifecycle cases exercise case variations; generic extension options have no observable behavior in the frozen target contract.

requirement: A sender lists connection-control field names in Connection where that protocol permits those fields.
notes: Need explicit sender audit for each generated connection-control field; HTTP/2 prohibition is separately inventoried.

requirement: Intermediaries remove Connection-nominated fields before forwarding.
notes: Targets are clients and origin servers, not forwarding proxies.

requirement: Intermediaries remove known hop-by-hop fields even without Connection nomination.
notes: Forwarding intermediaries are outside scope.

requirement: Senders do not nominate end-to-end fields as connection options.
notes: Arbitrary application-supplied fields and automatic sender behavior need a fidelity decision; no target-specific expected result is assumed.

requirement: A connection option need not have a corresponding field in the message.
notes: Need an explicit unknown-option acceptance case and subsequent exchange proving connection usability.

requirement: A connection-specific field without its option usually indicates improper intermediary forwarding.
notes: Advisory interpretation, with no unconditional endpoint rejection obligation.

requirement: Specification authors reserve names for new connection options.
notes: Registry and specification-author actions have no endpoint wire test.

requirement: The compress transfer coding uses the specified LZW format.
notes: Only when used as a transfer coding; independent valid/invalid compressed vectors and decoding order are not yet provided. Content-Encoding semantics are excluded.

requirement: The deflate transfer coding contains a zlib wrapper around a deflate stream.
notes: Only when used as a transfer coding; independent valid/invalid compressed vectors and decoding order are not yet provided. Content-Encoding semantics are excluded.

requirement: The gzip transfer coding uses the specified gzip representation and CRC.
notes: Only when used as a transfer coding; independent valid/invalid compressed vectors and decoding order are not yet provided. Content-Encoding semantics are excluded.

requirement: Recipients treat x-compress as equivalent to compress.
notes: Recommendation applies to transfer-coding use in this scope; no independent alias vectors yet.

requirement: Recipients treat x-gzip as equivalent to gzip.
notes: Recommendation applies to transfer-coding use in this scope; no independent alias vectors yet.

requirement: Status codes are three-digit integers with valid values 100 through 599.
notes: Current generated status-line cases sample 200 only; complete sender boundaries and HTTP/2 status mapping are not exhausted.

requirement: Clients understand the response class and treat unknown codes as x00 of that class.
notes: An exposed integer status alone cannot prove higher-level class treatment; general status semantics are excluded.

requirement: Clients receiving status outside 100 through 599 process it as a server-error response.
notes: Must distinguish permissive parsing from recommended semantic handling, without demanding rejection.

requirement: One request has zero or more informational responses followed by exactly one final response.
notes: Need wire association evidence across a subsequent request; merely returning interim status through a library API is insufficient proof.
